questionPico.intervention: Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily (active trial); observation off study drug with open-label SGLT2 inhibitor use allowed (post-trial follow-up)
questionPico.comparator: Placebo (randomised); original allocation groups compared by intention to treat in follow-up
questionPico.outcome: Durability of kidney and cardiovascular effects: kidney disease progression composite and components, eGFR slope, albuminuria, cardiovascular death / heart-failure hospitalisation / all-cause death, and safety across treatment and post-treatment periods

claims.claim: In the primary results report of EMPA-KIDNEY, the composite of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death occurred in 432 of 3304 participants (13.1%) in the empagliflozin group versus 558 of 3305 (16.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.64–0.82, P<0.001) over a median follow-up of 2.0 years.
claims.sourceTitle: Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
claims.supportQuote: During a median of 2.0 years follow-up, a primary outcome event occurred in 432 of 3304 patients (13.1%) in the empagliflozin group and in 558 of 3305 patients (16.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI 0.64 to 0.82; P<0.001)
claims.applicability: Adults with CKD at risk of progression meeting EMPA-KIDNEY eligibility (eGFR 20–<45 any ACR, or 45–<90 with ACR ≥200 mg/g).
claims.uncertainty: Effect estimate from a single randomised trial programme stopped early for efficacy at a median 2.0 years.

claims.uncertainty: Single randomised programme; follow-up truncated by early close-out at 2.0 years; slope is a surrogate endpoint.

supportingSources.sourceTitle: Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
supportingSources.supportQuote: During a median of 2.0 years follow-up, a primary outcome event occurred in 432 of 3304 patients (13.1%) in the empagliflozin group and in 558 of 3305 patients (16.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI 0.64 to 0.82; P<0.001) … In this population of patients with a wide range of causes of CKD, GFR and levels of albuminuria, empagliflozin safely reduced the risk of the primary outcome of kidney disease progression or death from cardiovascular causes by about 28%.

claims.claim: After empagliflozin was stopped, benefits persisted in attenuated form for up to about 12 months and then weakened: post-trial hazard ratio for the primary composite 0.87 (95% CI 0.76–0.99), most benefit in the first 6 months (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.38–0.93), first-year 0.76 (95% CI 0.60–0.96), second-year 0.90 (95% CI 0.75–1.07), while end-stage kidney disease remained reduced in the post-trial period (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66–0.98).
claims.applicability: EMPA-KIDNEY participants during a median 2.0 years of off-drug observation after ~2 years of treatment.
claims.uncertainty: Observational treatment context (no study drug, open-label SGLT2 inhibitor use 43% vs 40%); single programme; second-year and ESKD estimates are single estimates.

supportingSources.sourceTitle: Long-Term Effects of Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
supportingSources.supportQuote: During the entire follow-up period (active trial plus post-trial observation periods together), progression of kidney disease or death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 865 of 3304 patients (26.2%) in the empagliflozin group and in 1001 of 3305 (30.3%) in the placebo group (HR=0.79, 95%CI 0.72-0.87; Figure 1A ). This comprised a 28% overall reduction in risk during the active trial period (0.72, 0.64-0.82; 990 outcomes) and a 13% reduction during the post-trial period (0.87, 0.76-0.99; 876 additional first primary outcomes). Much of the post-trial benefit on the primary outcome occurred early: hazard ratios for the first and second years of follow-up post-trial were 0.76 (0.60-0.96) and 0.90 (0.75-1.07) respectively, with the hazard ratio for first 6 months 0.60 (0.38-0.93) ( Figure 1B ). … The effect on the primary outcome during the entire follow-up period included a 21% reduction in the risk of the secondary outcomes of kidney disease progression (23.5% vs. 27.1%: 0.79, 0.72-0.87; Table 3 & Figure S3 ), and a 26% reduction in ESKD (9.0% vs. 11.3%: 0.74, 0.64-0.87; Table S5 ). During the post-trial period, the hazard ratios for kidney disease progression and ESKD were 0.89 (0.77-1.02) and 0.80 (0.66-0.98), respectively ( Figure S3 ). … In summary, post-trial follow up of our trial participants quantified more completely the total effects of a short period of two years of empagliflozin treatment, including any carry-over effect after stopping study drug. In a broad range of patients with chronic kidney disease, empagliflozin continued to exert additional cardiorenal benefits for up to 12 months after it was discontinued.

claims.claim: Across the programme no new or late safety hazard was measured: within the trial, rates of serious adverse events were broadly similar between groups, ketoacidosis was rare (6 vs 1 events; 0.09 vs 0.02 per 100 patient-years) and concentrated in insulin-treated participants with diabetes, serious acute kidney injury was not increased (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.60–1.00), and lower-limb amputations were reported as event counts (28 vs 19; mainly in diabetic kidney disease) with too few events for reliable effect estimates outside diabetic kidney disease; in the post-trial period adverse events were not collected and the pre-specified safety outcome of non-cardiovascular death did not differ between groups (HR 0.97, 0.79–1.20).
claims.uncertainty: In-trial safety outcomes robust; amputation events reported as counts with no significance test stated and too few events for reliable estimates in non-diabetic causes; post-trial absence of adverse-event capture means off-treatment safety is unmeasured rather than established.

supportingSources.sourceTitle: Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
supportingSources.supportQuote: Ketoacidosis occurred in 6 patients in the empagliflozin group versus 1 patient in the placebo group (0.09 versus 0.02 per 100 patient-years). Lower limb amputations occurred in 28 patients in the empagliflozin group and 19 in the placebo group (0.43 versus 0.29 per 100 patient-years). The incidence of serious urinary tract infections, hyperkalemia, acute kidney injuries, serious or symptomatic dehydrations, liver injuries, and bone fractures were broadly similar in each group ( Tables 2 and S7 ). There was no apparent evidence that empagliflozin increased the incidence of serious adverse events overall, or in any particular MedDRA system organ class ( Table S8 ).

supportingSources.sourceTitle: Impact of Primary Kidney Disease on the Effects of Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease: Secondary Analyses of the EMPA-KIDNEY Trial
supportingSources.supportQuote: Overall, empagliflozin had no significant effects on risk of serious acute kidney injury (HR 0·78; 95% CI 0·60 to 1·00), with similar results across the four main categories of cause of kidney disease (P for heterogeneity=0·28; Supplementary Table 6 ). Ketoacidosis occurred in 6 participants allocated to empagliflozin (including five participants on insulin, one of whom had type 1 diabetes, and one participant without diabetes) and one allocated to placebo (who was not taking open-label SGLT2 inhibitor). There were 28 vs 19 lower-limb amputation events in the empagliflozin vs placebo groups, respectively (including 20 vs 14 toe amputations). These two safety outcomes mainly occurred among participants with diabetic kidney disease with too few events to provide reliable estimates of any effect in participants with non-diabetic causes of kidney disease.

supportingSources.sourceTitle: Long-Term Effects of Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
supportingSources.supportQuote: Post-trial follow-up aimed to collect additional efficacy and cause-specific mortality outcome data. … Tertiary outcomes were death from any cause and, separately, death from cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular causes (the latter being the safety outcome for post-trial follow-up); and the primary outcome assessed by key subgroups of interest. … During the entire follow-up period, there was a reduction in the risk of death from a cardiovascular cause by 25% (3.8% vs. 4.9%: 0.75, 0.59-0.95) and no material effect on non-cardiovascular mortality (5.3% vs. 5.3%: 0.97, 0.79-1.20), meaning there were 301 (9.1%) vs. 336 (10.2%) deaths from any cause (0.86, 0.74-1.01; Table 3 and Figure S5 ).

claims.applicability: EMPA-KIDNEY trial design and analysis, as reported in the main results report.
